question: Which BLAS preference produces stable and faster rank-16 LoRA weight gradients while the forward preference is held at Lt?
inputs: Synthetic BF16 inputs with frozen-training LoRA rank 16 and previous Qwen observed token counts and projection extents. Isolated A and B linear weights; no model weights or scaled/dropout training trajectory.
design: One eight-card pilot, then 76 qualified idle nodes. Per-card ABBA or BAAB, two warmups and 256 calls per block, with a rounded FP32 weight-gradient reference and the inherited 0.0625 maximum absolute gate. Keep every failed card in the denominator.
timing_scope: Device event envelope includes host preference setter and weight-gradient dispatch. Independent sysfs driver busy samples.
qualification: API preference readback only; kernel identity and model numerical acceptance remain unverified.
